title: The Horizon of the Sepik Basin
premise: Jude Almeida flies a battered Cessna through Papua New Guinea's Sepik Basin, hauling medicine, mail, and secrets for scattered mission stations and mining camps. When prospector Elias Wren crash-lands at Jude's airstrip with a bullet wound and a map to a lost alluvial gold field inside the highlands, he trades it for a promise: deliver it to his estranged daughter, Mara, before a corrupt mining syndicate's enforcers find it. Jude and Mara are forced to trek over the range ahead of the snows, racing the brief window when glacier calving opens a high pass. Betrayed by a guide in the syndicate's pay, hunted through river gorges and cloud forest, they discover the map's true treasure is evidence of the syndicate's massacre of a village that claimed the same ground. In the climax at the calving glacier, Jude chooses love and justice over the invisibility that kept them alive, delivering the evidence to a tribal court that operates outside any national law; the syndicate's men are judged by the people they wronged, and Jude and Mara, no longer running, build a life at the airstrip where the wilderness finally lets them stay.
about_author: Petra Amberdale is the pen name of a former aid-flight logistics coordinator who spent six years organizing supply runs across remote Melanesia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose loyalties are tested by geography, and she still refuses to fly in anything with fewer than two engines.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rain, and Rumors
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Establishes the Sepik airstrip, the rhythm of supply flights, and the fragile neutrality Jude maintains by knowing everyone and belonging to no one. A missionary warns that men from the Kavera Mining Consortium are buying silence upriver. Emotional beat: the comfort of deliberate isolation, with hairline cracks showing.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fell Out of the Sky
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A damaged aircraft limps onto Jude's strip at dusk; the pilot, Elias Wren, is bleeding out. He presses a oilskin-wrapped map into Jude's hands and makes him swear to carry it to his daughter Mara in Wewak. Emotional beat: a promise extracted under pressure that Jude instantly regrets.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with flashback to Elias's last coherent words. Jude examines the map and realizes it marks ground the Kavera Consortium already leases—and ground where a village was erased from every record. Emotional beat: dread, as neutrality becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Mara Wren
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In Wewak, Mara works at a coastal trading post, estranged from the father who abandoned her for gold country. Jude arrives with the map and the news of his death. Emotional beat: grief curdling into anger—at Elias, at Jude, at being handed a dead man's war.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A polished Kavera representative offers to 'buy' the map for a generous sum, then makes the threat explicit when she refuses. Jude witnesses the exchange. Emotional beat: the mask of legality slipping off corporate violence.

chapters.title: Two Tickets Out
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude and Mara flee Wewak by night in the Cessna, dodging a syndicate informant at the fuel depot. In the air, they argue about everything except what's growing between them. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership forged in adrenaline.

chapters.title: The Guide with Two Names
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They land at a river town and hire Toma, a charismatic guide who claims to know the high pass. Mara distrusts him; Jude wants to. Emotional beat: uneasy trust, the reader's first quiet hint that Toma's loyalties are for sale.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. By dugout canoe through the Sepik's tributaries, the trio passes villages that go silent at the mention of Kavera. Mara learns from an old woman that her father once paid the village's debts—her first glimpse of who Elias really was. Emotional beat: grief softening into complicated love.

chapters.title: Cloud Forest
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They abandon the canoe and climb into cloud forest; leeches, rot, and a near-fatal river crossing bind the three travelers. Jude confesses the promise to Elias and their own history of running from accountability. Emotional beat: vulnerability traded for trust.

chapters.title: The Erased Village
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They reach the ruins of the village that once held the gold field—burned two years ago, survivors scattered. A survivor recognizes the map and reveals Elias witnessed the massacre and had been running from Kavera ever since. Emotional beat: the map transforms from treasure to testimony.

chapters.title: Toma's Night Market
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. At a highland waystation, Toma secretly radios the Consortium's enforcers, bargaining for his brother, whom Kavera holds in a labor camp. Emotional beat: betrayal with a human face; Toma believes he's saving one life by spending two.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Saddle
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Enforcers ambush the party at a mountain saddle. Toma's warning shot—fired wide on purpose—gives Jude and Mara seconds to escape into scree. Emotional beat: shock, betrayal, and the bitter arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Cold Above the Trees
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Above the tree line, the race against the snows turns lethal. Frostbite, thin air, and Mara's injury slow them; Jude carries her through a whiteout night. Emotional beat: love admitted aloud for the first time, in the worst possible place.

chapters.title: What Toma Carried
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. Toma, wracked with guilt, follows their trail and brings medicine and the enforcers' route plan, asking nothing. Jude must decide whether to forgive or to use him. Emotional beat: the cost of justice—mercy that might get them killed.

chapters.title: The Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The glacier begins to calve; the pass will be crossable for perhaps three days. Through binoculars they watch enforcers massing at the far side. Emotional beat: the window opening like a trap snapping shut behind them.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The ice crossing itself—crevasses, a bridge of glacier ice collapsing behind them, Toma leading them through a route only he knows. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into something like grace; the three become a unit.

chapters.title: The High Valley Court
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They descend into the hidden valley where massacre survivors and their allies hold territory outside government reach, governed by a council of elders and clan law. Mara presents the map and her father's testimony. Emotional beat: awe and fear—justice here is real, and it is not gentle.

chapters.title: The Judgment of the Elders
chapters.summary: Elder Kombai's POV. The council weighs the evidence, the survivors' testimony, and the arrival of Kavera's enforcers at the valley mouth. They rule: the enforcers will be tried by the people they wronged. Emotional beat: law older than any nation, cold and certain.

chapters.title: The Stand at the Pass
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The climax. Enforcers push into the valley; Jude, Mara, Toma, and the valley's defenders hold the pass through a night battle, using the terrain the glacier carved. Toma takes a bullet saving Mara. Emotional beat: courage without glory, blood on stone.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The surviving enforcers face the council's judgment; the Consortium's local operation collapses as evidence travels downriver to journalists and missionaries. Toma's brother is freed. Emotional beat: justice delivered outside the law, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Airstrip
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Weeks later, Jude and Mara rebuild the airstrip together, the Cessna patched, the map framed on the wall—not as treasure but as testimony. Elias is buried in the valley he wronged and redeemed. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.

chapters.title: First Light, First Flight
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Dawn: Mara takes her first flying lesson over the basin, and Jude, for the first time, isn't flying to disappear. A new rumor arrives by radio—there's always another map, another promise—but this time they'll face it together. Emotional beat: love and duty no longer at war; the horizon open.
